paper: Ravfogel, Twiton, Goldberg, Cotterell. Linear Adversarial Concept Erasure (R-LACE). ICML 2022, PMLR 162:18400-18421
date_version: PMLR 2022-06-28 PDF (read in full); arXiv 2201.12091 v8 2024-12-17 (correction passages read)
question_scope: Remove a rank-k linear concept subspace by orthogonal projection so that linear predictors cannot recover the concept (post-hoc, fixed representations)
method_coverage: R-LACE (Fantope relaxation of min-max over rank-k orthogonal projections); closed form for linear regression/PLS; INLP, PCA (Bolukbasi), BERT gradient-reversal adversaries as baselines
task_utility_protocol: Profession accuracy with a linear head refit on projected BERT [CLS]; SimLex-999; adversary checkpoint chosen by maximum dev loss of a fresh linear classifier; 5 runs mean±sd
attacker_access: Labelled projected representations; linear SVM/logistic at test; RBF-SVM and MLP(128) on GloVe; no knowledge of P; single release
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: Nonlinear: one sentence, GloVe only (RBF-SVM and MLP recover gender >90%). Adaptive/defense-aware: none. Fresh adversaries recover 99%+ after gradient-reversal training (Table 2 fn 9)
task_output_eval: No (task accuracy and TPR-GAP fairness only; outputs not attacked for S)
statistical_treatment: 5 random restarts, mean±sd; WEAT p-values; no CIs on accuracy
overlap_durable_guarantees: Repeats: linear certificate passes while nonlinear/fresh attackers recover; AAAI extends to 67 certificate-approved tabular configurations, defense-aware tier, output surface, utility bar. Not cited by AAAI (AAAI cites only the EMNLP kernel paper)
overlap_pcrl: PCRL's linear-R2 guardedness is in this family; PCRL rank proposition credits RLACE framing. PCRL bib key ravfogel2022rlace has wrong authors (adds Belrose, Gonen) and duplicates ravfogel2022linear; related work wrongly calls R-LACE a subsequent oblique-projection refinement
possible_additional_value: Primary citation for 'linear erasure does not stop nonlinear recovery' and for 'adversarial training does not generalise to fresh adversaries'. Cite the v8 correction (game is convex-convex, max-min order)
supporting_locations: p.6 §5.1 (nonlinear >90%); p.7 Table 2 + fn 9; p.13 App. B.1; p.3 Prop. 3.1; p.15-16 App. B.4, B.6-B.7; arXiv v8 §2.3 fn 4

paper: Ravfogel, Vargas, Goldberg, Cotterell. Adversarial Concept Erasure in Kernel Space (PDF title: Kernelized Concept Erasure). EMNLP 2022, pp. 6034-6055
question_scope: Kernelize the linear erasure game to remove nonlinearly encoded concepts; test whether a single RKHS exhaustively removes gender (exhaustive RKHS hypothesis)
method_coverage: Kernelized min-max (representer lemma, Nystrom L=1024) plus a pre-image MLP; kernels Poly, RBF, Laplace, Linear, Sigmoid, EasyMKL, UniformMK
task_utility_protocol: SimLex-999 (0.400 -> 0.387-0.396); Bios profession accuracy with a linear head (76.93 -> 74.19, RBF only); P chosen by maximum drop in a linear classifier on eval; 4 runs
attacker_access: Labelled pre-images; exact-kernel SVMs (same kernel = defense-matched); transfer kernels; MLP(128); single release
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: Yes, nonlinear: same-kernel partial protection (0.49-0.75), no transfer (MLP 0.97 for every neutralizing kernel). Not adaptive beyond a matched kernel
overlap_durable_guarantees: Cited (ravfogel2022kernelized). AAAI's MMD/HSIC kernel-projection failures and Obliviator failure repeat non-transfer; AAAI extends with tiers, outputs, utility
overlap_pcrl: Not cited; implies PCRL cannot upgrade a linear R2 bound to a nonlinear claim with a single kernel/HSIC term
possible_additional_value: Primary citation for 'nonlinear erasure against one class does not transfer'. Reviewer's 'Ravfogel et al. 2022' is ambiguous between this and R-LACE; cite both

paper: Elazar, Ravfogel, Jacovi, Goldberg. Amnesic Probing: Behavioral Explanation with Amnesic Counterfactuals. TACL 9:160-175 (2021)
question_scope: CAUSAL USE: does a model use property Z for its task? Remove Z (INLP) and measure the behaviour change. Explicitly not a recoverability question
method_coverage: INLP removal of linear information; Rand (random-direction) and Selectivity (re-inject gold property) controls; layer-wise interventions
task_utility_protocol: Task = BERT masked/non-masked word prediction (LM accuracy, D_KL); INLP stopped at majority+1 on dev
attacker_access: Not applicable (no adversary); linear SVM probes
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: No (linear removal only; authors caution against causal over-interpretation)
task_output_eval: Yes, as BEHAVIOUR (the model's own predictions change), not as attribute recovery
statistical_treatment: No seeds or CIs; Spearman correlation probe-acc vs importance (p=0.871)
overlap_durable_guarantees: AAAI measures recoverability, not use (consistent), but cites Elazar for 'what a probe finds depends on the probe' (mismatch). The title 'Outputs Leak What They Use' implies use; no amnesic intervention is run
overlap_pcrl: PCRL's R2 bound is recoverability; its 'access prohibited' motivation is a use/access notion that it does not test. §7.1 re-recovery at later layers is a caution for erase-layer placement
possible_additional_value: Provides the design (intervention plus Rand/Selectivity controls) needed if any 'use' claim is made about outputs; keep use and recoverability as separate claims

paper: Song & Shmatikov. Overlearning Reveals Sensitive Attributes. ICLR 2020
question_scope: Recoverability/privacy: models trained for simple tasks learn weakly correlated sensitive attributes; inference from representations and re-purposing; censoring fails
method_coverage: Censoring by adversarial training (Xie et al.) and information-theoretic VAE (Moyer et al.); de-censoring attack; re-purposing by fine-tuning layers; inner-layer censoring
task_utility_protocol: Target accuracy on a held-out 20%; fixed censoring hyperparameters plus sweeps; no seeds
attacker_access: Auxiliary labelled data (50% of train size), black-box encoder E; de-censoring uses an auxiliary uncensored model; re-purposing needs weights
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: Yes, nonlinear MLP attackers (same architecture as the censor). Partly adaptive (de-censoring). Not given censor parameters
multiple_release_eval: No (PIPA uses pairs of representations, not multiple releases)
overlap_durable_guarantees: Cited. Repeats: approved/censored representations leak to fresh attackers; stronger censoring is not monotone. Complements: Song's pairs have low Cramer's V while AAAI output leakage tracks coupling
overlap_pcrl: Cited (intro). Inner-layer result implies PCRL's bound is moot if backbone features or weights are released
possible_additional_value: Representation leakage is decoupled from label-attribute coupling; layer-wise re-purposing threat model
full_text_reading_status: main text read, appendix not available (none in arXiv v3); OpenReview camera-ready not compared
supporting_locations: p.3 §3.1 Alg. 1; p.4 Table 1; p.5 Table 2 §4.2; p.6 Fig. 2, Table 3; p.7-8 Tables 4-5; p.9-10 §6

paper: Stadler, Kulynych, Gastpar, Papernot, Troncoso. The Fundamental Limits of Least-Privilege Learning. ICML 2024, PMLR 235:46393-46411
date_version: PMLR 2024-07-08 PDF (read in full); arXiv 2402.12235v2 fetched
question_scope: Formalise least privilege (purpose limitation) as bounded maximal leakage about ALL attributes given the true label; impossibility under a strictly positive posterior
method_coverage: Theory (Thm 1-2, Prop. 1-2); empirics with ERM, gradient-reversal censoring, MAX-ENT, gradients, hidden layers, ResNet-18, TabNet
task_utility_protocol: Utility I_inf(Y;Z) = log normalised accuracy on eval split; 5 repetitions
attacker_access: Bayes-optimal in theory; empirically Random Forest on (z, y) with black-box f_E and 20% auxiliary data; label-only adversary
task_output_eval: Label-only (true Y) fundamental leakage measured (Fig. 3); trained-model predictions not attacked as a separate surface
overlap_durable_guarantees: Cited. AAAI 'label-coupling predictor' = Stadler's label-only/fundamental leakage (already measured, §4.1 Fig. 3), so 'we contribute its measurement' overclaims; 'leakage floor established by Stadler' is imprecise. AAAI adds the link to output leakage and removal cost
overlap_pcrl: Not cited despite the purpose-limitation framing. Theorem quantifies over all attributes (incl. constructed S*), so it does not prohibit PCRL's finite declared-set linear bound but forbids an LPP claim
possible_additional_value: Exact framing for which claims about a finite declared S are possible; label-only baseline is the correct comparator for output leakage
supporting_locations: p.2 Assumption A; p.4 Def. 1, Thm 1; p.4-5 Def. 2, eq. 8-9, Thm 2, Prop. 1; p.7 §4.1 Fig. 3; p.8 Fig. 4; p.9 §5; p.12-14 App. A (Def. 4, Prop. 3, proofs)

paper: Taylor, Vippathalla, Coon. Adaptive Privacy of Sequential Data Releases Under Collusion. arXiv 2601.21859 (preprint)
date_version: arXiv v2 2026-07-10 (read in full); v1 2026-01-29 not read
question_scope: Online sequential releases to m parties; per-party MI budget I(Rk;X)<=eps_k and collusion budget I(Rk,R^{k-1};X)<=delta_k; maximise distortion or MI utility
method_coverage: Blahut-Arimoto-style channel design (finite alphabets, known joint pmf); adaptive conditioning on previous releases; non-adaptive and symmetric-channel baselines

attacker_access: Information-theoretic (MI to the whole X); worst-case colluder pools all previous releases; no learned attacker

paper: Gitiaux & Rangwala. Learning Smooth and Fair Representations (AGWN). AISTATS 2021, PMLR 130:253-261
date_version: PMLR 2021-03-18; main PDF and supplementary PDF read in full
question_scope: When can a finite-sample demographic-parity certificate of a representation bound ALL downstream binary test functions? Necessary: finite chi2-MI; sufficient: additive Gaussian noise
method_coverage: AGWN autoencoder with a plug-in Gaussian-mixture DP loss (no adversary); baselines AdvCE (Edwards & Storkey), AdvL1 (LAFTR-style)
task_utility_protocol: Reconstruction loss vs 95th-quantile processor disparity; Adult income accuracy vs DP for varied downstream nets; sigma tuned on validation; 50 repeats per lambda
attacker_access: Downstream MLPs (2-4 hidden layers) trained on fresh noisy representations with S labels; single draw per input
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: Nonlinear MLPs; certificate in theory covers all test functions of one draw (incl. defense-aware); no multi-draw or side-information attacker
task_output_eval: Covered by post-processing for binary outputs computed from Z; empirically DP of income classifiers
statistical_treatment: 50 repeats per lambda scatter; expectation-only bound whose constant exp(||t||^2/2sigma^2) is vacuous at the paper's sigma (my computation)
overlap_durable_guarantees: Not cited. AAAI certified full-rank channel (clip + Gaussian, GDP ceiling) is the same mechanism type; AAAI Prop. 2 is related to Gitiaux Thm 2.1; 18.2% adversarial-certificate failure anticipates AAAI's 59/67
overlap_pcrl: Not cited. Thm 2.1 implies a deterministic h_p cannot carry a finite-sample all-test-function certificate; PCRL's linear R2 is not upgradeable without smoothing
possible_additional_value: Certified-noise baseline missing from AAAI; definition of the certified quantity (1-2BER*) maps directly to attribute inference

paper: Tang, Hosseini, Zhai, Durand, Mori. FairNVT: Fair Classification via Noise Injection in Vision Transformers (v1 title: Improving Fairness via Noise Injection in Vision Transformers)
date_version: arXiv 2604.16780 v2 2026-08-17 (header: Published in TMLR 08/2026; read in full); v1 2026-04-18 (arXiv comment: ICLR 2026 AFAA Workshop; skimmed)
question_scope: Fair classification from frozen transformer encoders: split task/sensitive adapters, clipped Gaussian noise on the sensitive branch, orthogonality+HSIC and DP losses
method_coverage: FairNVT vs Vanilla, ViT-FSCL, FairViT, FairVPT, FairNet (vision); FT-Debias, INLP, SUP, ConGater, DAM (BIOS)
task_utility_protocol: Acc/BAcc; config with highest validation accuracy (3 runs, mean(sd)); Pareto curves over all configs on test
attacker_access: MLP attacker on embeddings (same architecture as head), trained on train split; deeper MLPs; averaging over 5/50 noise draws; not defense-aware
nonlinear_or_adaptive_eval: Nonlinear MLPs up to 10 hidden layers; not defense-aware; repeated-draw averaging (Avg50 recovers 92.5%)
